## 0.269.0 — 2026-08-06

### Changed
- **Turbopack everywhere: the production build drops `--webpack`** — the handbrake on since 80f8ed7 (2026-05-13, "until @serwist/turbopack is stable") is fully off. `@serwist/next` (webpack-injection architecture) is REPLACED by `@serwist/turbopack` 9.5.12, which works completely differently: the SW is bundled by esbuild inside a force-static Route Handler (`app/serwist/[path]/route.ts`, new — serves `/serwist/sw.js` + sourcemap with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` so the nested URL still controls the origin) and registered EXPLICITLY by `components/SerwistRegister.tsx` (new, `SerwistProvider` from `@serwist/turbopack/react`; same flags the old `withSerwistInit` carried; dev stays disabled — the localhost stale-SW landmine) mounted in all three root layouts. `app/sw.ts` now imports `defaultCache` from `@serwist/turbopack/worker`; the new `withSerwist` wrapper only adds esbuild to `serverExternalPackages`. Deps: `@serwist/next` removed, `esbuild-wasm` added (the package uses native esbuild on Windows, wasm elsewhere — CI is Linux). **Verified end-to-end locally:** Turbopack `next build` exit 0 with the SW bundled (127 precache entries) and `● /serwist/[path]` prerendered; **`opennextjs-cloudflare build` exit 0, worker saved** (the compatibility question answered — the Cloudflare pipeline accepts Turbopack output); served build returns `/serwist/sw.js` 200 `application/javascript` + `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` with push handlers + precache manifest in the bundle. **PREVIEW-GATED for the deploy-level half:** installed-PWA update rollover from `/sw.js` → `/serwist/sw.js` (same scope `/`, new script URL; `skipWaiting:false` means it lands on the next-after-next launch) + push still subscribing on a real deploy — operator click-through before/after merge. Migration note: installed clients keep the OLD /sw.js worker until the new registration wins the scope; `public/sw.js` is no longer emitted, so the old script 404s on update checks, which browsers treat as "keep waiting" then replace via the new register() call.

## 0.255.1 — 2026-08-04

### Fixed
- **Push subscriptions no longer depend on a build-time key — and the lost VAPID public key recovers itself.** The key existed ONLY as a write-only worker runtime secret (unreadable back; not in any env file, repo, or git history; the Vercel copy died with the account), while the client needed it INLINED at build (`NEXT_PUBLIC_*`), which is why every Workers build shipped push compiled out ("Server isn't configured for push yet"). Now `/api/push/status` serves the PUBLIC key (public by design — every subscriber's browser holds a copy; the private key never leaves the server), `subscribeToPush()` fetches it at subscribe time (inlined var kept as a zero-fetch fast path), `getPushAvailability()` is capability-only, and the settings banner derives from server truth (`vapidConfigured`). Side effect: the key is now readable from the endpoint for the record, and per-dev workers need no VAPID build variable ever.

## 0.255.0 — 2026-08-03

### Fixed
- **On-demand revalidation works on Cloudflare (operator pick: "DO").** `open-next.config.ts` never set a `tagCache`, leaving the adapter dummy in place — `writeTags` a silent `return;`, `isStale` always false — so every `revalidatePath`/`revalidateTag` on prod (blog publish, approve-inline, author-profile edits) did nothing; staleness was bounded only by the 300 s ISR window + ≤30 min regional cache (proven, session 26). Now: `doShardedTagCache({ baseShardSize: 4, regionalCache: true })` — Durable Objects, no new storage product; the `DOShardedTagCache` class already rode `worker.ts`'s re-exports. All four wrangler configs gain the `NEXT_TAG_CACHE_DO_SHARDED` binding + a `v2` sqlite-class migration. The per-shard regional cache (5 s TTL) bounds revalidation visibility at ~5 s, which is the contract the publish path wants.

## 0.254.0 — 2026-08-03

### Fixed
- **The landing LCP disaster (mobile 15.3 s, PSI 2026-08-03 baseline).** Three compounding causes in `CircuitSlideshow`: all seven hero photos mounted eagerly (4,112 KiB of raw ~1900px JPEGs served under `images: unoptimized`), the LCP preload carried no priority hint, and everything queued behind CSS on slow links. Now: the seven circuit photos are 1600w WebP q78 (**4,112 → 1,673 KiB total**, monaco 979 → 476), the slideshow mounts ONLY the active + outgoing slide (initial page load fetches ONE ~190 KiB image; each next slide fetches at its turn), and slide 0 carries `fetchPriority="high"` on both the img and its preload (verified in the SSR HTML). The crossfade behavior is unchanged — the outgoing slide stays mounted through the fade. Est. mobile LCP → ~2.5-3 s; re-measure per the perf-baselines protocol after 24 h.

## 0.248.0 — 2026-08-03

### Added
- **`in_review`: drafts are finally private, and submitting is an explicit act** (migration `20260803120000_post_in_review.sql`, applied by the operator). `draft` had been doing two jobs — a writer's private workspace *and* the review queue — and because `POST /api/blog` notified on every insert, saving half a paragraph pinged the operator. Writers responded by not saving, which is the opposite of what a draft is for. Now `draft` notifies nobody, `in_review` is a deliberate submission that fires the existing admin email + push, and `approved`/`published`/`rejected` are unchanged. This is WordPress's "Pending Review" and Ghost's contributor model, both of which separate "can write" from "can publish" the same way. The constraint was dropped and recreated because Postgres has no ALTER for a check expression; its current definition was read from `pg_constraint` first rather than assumed, confirming the widening cannot invalidate an existing row.
- **`submitPost`** (`lib/blog.ts`), guarded to `draft` only with an exact count, so a double-submit is a no-op rather than a second notification and a decided post cannot be dragged back into the queue. Exposed as `action: 'submit'` on `POST /api/blog/[id]`, which is now the **only** path that alerts the operator.
- **The author finally hears back.** `notifyAuthorDecision` (`lib/blog-notify.ts`) emails the writer on approve or reject, carrying the scheduled publish time rendered in Europe/Athens with the zone named. `decidePost` previously flipped the status and notified nobody, so a writer had to poll the console to learn whether their work was going live. Email only, deliberately: a contributor is not necessarily a push subscriber, and a timestamp does not fit a notification body. New `blog-decision` ledger kind, keyed per post **and** per outcome+time, so a reschedule legitimately re-notifies with the new time while a retry of the same decision cannot double-send. Fires in `after()`, so a mail hiccup can never fail the decision that has already been committed.
- **Three queues in the blog console** (`inReview` added to `GET /api/blog` and `PostModeration`): private drafts with a "Submit for review" button, submissions awaiting a decision, and scheduled posts. A writer sees their submission's state and is told they can still edit it; only an admin gets the approve/reject controls.

### Changed
- **A writer can no longer approve their own post.** `authorizePostActor` granted a writer every action on a post they own, which included `approve` — so a writer could schedule and therefore publish their own work, quietly bypassing the approval SOP the whole blog process is built on. Deciding is now admin-only; submitting is the writer's action. This is a deliberate tightening and the point of the review state.
- **`updatePostContent` accepts `in_review`.** A submitted piece stays editable while it waits, which is the difference between submitting and publishing; `published` and `rejected` remain locked. The existing test asserting the old two-status contract was updated to the new one rather than loosened.
- **`scripts/draft-post.mts` submits after creating.** A script-authored post arrives finished, so leaving it as a private draft would hide it from the operator's queue — the opposite of what that script is for.

### Notes
- **Correcting an earlier claim in this changelog's own voice:** the publish lag is bounded at roughly **15 minutes**, not the ~20 previously stated. `app/api/cron/publish-posts/route.ts:42-43` already calls `revalidatePath` for `/blog` and each published post, so there is no 300-second ISR tail to add; and approving a post whose time has already passed publishes it inline and immediately (`app/api/blog/[id]/route.ts:105-116`). The only remaining lever is the `*/15` cron cadence in `worker.ts:30`.

## 0.247.0 — 2026-07-31

### Added
- **All 488 generated champion pages are now indexable, taking the information hub from 310 indexed entries to ~783.** Previously only the current champion per series was `featured`, so 473 pages rendered `noindex` — which is what Search Console was reporting as "Excluded by 'noindex' tag", and the "validation Failed" simply meant Google re-checked and found them still noindexed. Working as designed, but keeping real answers invisible. `generated.ts` now features every champion entry, and `INFORMATION_MAX_INDEXED` rises 323 → 900 (roughly seven seasons of headroom at ~15 new champion pages a year; the `console.warn` on exceeding it is untouched).
- **Why this is not the "scaled content" shape the cap was built to prevent**, measured across all 488 before flipping: shortest body **188** characters, median **316**, longest **495**, and not one is a single sentence — each names the champion, their machine or team, the secondary title and title-count context, with every fact traceable to a vetted `content/series/<slug>/champions.json`. The cap was raised rather than removed, because what it still guards is genuinely low-quality bulk.
- **The two `most-*` record pages for F2 and F3 stay unfeatured deliberately.** That gate is `hasStableName(meta)`, a factual guard rather than an indexing one: both series were rebranded from GP2/GP3, so a "most titles" aggregate would silently merge two different championships.
- **`lib/champions-integrity.test.ts`** — invariants across every curated `champions.json`: unique plausible years, every row names a driver, the champion outscores the runner-up, the runner-up is a different person, `runnerUpTeam` is not a bare number or a model designation, and counts are non-negative integers. 91 assertions.

### Notes
- **The MotoGP 1949-2015 enrichment was attempted and deliberately abandoned, unshipped.** Points/wins/runner-up were extracted from Wikipedia season articles by a deterministic parser (no number through a model), cross-checked against the independently curated champion names already in the repo. That check rejected **13 of 63** parsed rows — each naming a real champion of a *different* class that season with plausible points attached (1949 Frith for Graham, 1963-65 Redman for Hailwood, 1966 Hailwood for Agostini). Of the 50 survivors, two were then spot-checked against a second source: 1993 confirmed exactly (Schwantz 248 points, 4 wins), but **1975 conflicted** — the season article gives Agostini 84 points and 4 wins, his own article gives 70 and 3, most likely the era's dropped-scores rule reporting gross versus net. A 50% failure rate on the verification sample means the remaining 48 rows cannot be trusted, so nothing was written: `content/series/motogp/champions.json` is byte-identical to before. The parser, the fetched wikitext and the name cross-check pattern are the reusable part; the conclusion is that this content needs genuine two-source verification per row, not a single-source parse.

## 0.246.2 — 2026-07-31

### Fixed
- **Authors without a profile photo got Clerk's generic grey avatar instead of our initial tile.** `resolveAuthorIdentity` trusted `imageUrl`, which Clerk **always** populates — with no uploaded photo it serves its own generated placeholder, so the editorial fallback could never render. Observed live on `/authors`: the Greek contributor's row showed Clerk's default. Now gated on `hasImage`, which is the only way to tell an uploaded photo from a generated one. The KV cache key gained a `v2:` segment in the same change, because entries written before the gate had already cached the placeholder as a real image and a plain key reuse would have served the old behaviour for up to an hour; v1 entries expire on their own TTL.

### Changed
- **`CLAUDE.md` landmine #2 corrected — it had been telling every reader the opposite of the truth.** It said middleware is `proxy.ts`, not `middleware.ts`. The repo has `middleware.ts` and no `proxy.ts`: the Cloudflare migration renamed it back because OpenNext needs the Edge runtime. Next 16 prefers `proxy.ts` and warns `The "middleware" file convention is deprecated` on every build, so the landmine now states that the warning is expected and must not be "fixed" on sight, since renaming without confirming OpenNext support breaks the deploy. The stack table's `app/` row was stale too (it named `proxy.ts` and omitted the `(admin)` route group).

### Notes
- **Investigated, not fixed, with findings recorded so the next attempt starts ahead:** (1) `/authors` builds as `ƒ` (dynamic) while `/blog` builds as `○` (prerendered) despite doing comparable work; the only meaningful difference is the `clerkClient()` call inside `resolveAuthorIdentity`, but `/authors/[slug]` calls it too and *does* prerender, so that explanation is incomplete and each experiment costs a ~4 minute build. (2) The `metadataBase` warning fires **20 times per build** even though all three root layouts (`(app)`, `(marketing)`, `(admin)`) set it; the only two routes outside those groups are `app/offline/page.tsx` (exports no metadata) and `app/opengraph-image.tsx`, which does not account for 20. Next does not name the offending routes in the warning.

## 0.246.1 — 2026-07-31

### Fixed
- **Published blog posts were absent from the sitemap entirely.** `lib/sitemap-data.ts` advertised `/blog` but not one post on it, so the site's most original content was discoverable only by crawling the index — which is precisely the "Crawled - currently not indexed" shape sitting in Search Console. Now emits every published post from both sources the `/blog` page merges (DB posts via `publishedPosts`, legacy MDX via `loadAllPosts`), deduped by slug with the DB winning to match that page's own precedence, sorted for deterministic build-to-build output. ## 0.246.0 — 2026-07-31

### Added
- **Public author pages at `/authors` and `/authors/<slug>`, and the author's own editor at `/settings/author`.** There was no author surface of any kind: `post.author_id` held a Clerk id, the byline resolved a name + avatar from Clerk on the post page and stopped there, so nothing tied a writer's work together and nothing gave search engines a person to attribute it to. New table `author` (migration `20260728120000_author.sql`), keyed on `clerk_user_id` (unique, FK to `app_user`) so it joins the account on one side and `post.author_id` on the other **without** a second FK from `post` — a writer has to be able to draft before anyone has written their profile, and `canPreviewUnpublished` compares `post.author_id` against the live Clerk session id, so the Clerk id stays the join key on both sides. `bio` is `not null` deliberately: no row means no page, which is what stops an empty author stub existing at all. `slug` is a column rather than a derived value because `lib/slug.ts` `slugify` strips everything outside `[a-z0-9]` and returns `""` for a non-Latin display name (probed: `slugify('Παναγιώτης Λουτριώτης')` → `''`).
- **Self-service profiles.** `PUT /api/author` (writer-or-admin, rate-limited 20/10min per user) upserts the caller's own row — keyed on their Clerk id, so there is no path to another author's profile — and revalidates `/authors`, both the new and the previous `/authors/<slug>` (a slug change otherwise leaves the old URL cached), and `/blog`. Validation lives in a new pure `lib/author-profile.ts` **without** a DB import, because `components/author/AuthorProfileForm` needs the same limits and importing `lib/authors.ts` would drag the service-role Supabase client into a client bundle: slug `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`, 3-40 chars; name 2-80; bio 40-1200 (the minimum is the thin-content guard on an indexable page); up to 6 links, https-only, labels ≤24. A link the author filled in that sanitisation would drop fails the whole save rather than vanishing silently. `role_title` is **not** author-editable: it is the masthead label, and a new contributor must not be able to self-title.
- **Per-post profile visibility** (migration `20260728130000_post_hide_on_author_page.sql`): `post.hide_on_author_page`, toggled by the owning author from their own screen. It hides a post from their profile only — the post stays live at `/blog/<slug>`, in the feed and in the sitemap. `setAuthorPostVisibility` filters both UPDATEs on `author_id = <caller>` so a forged id cannot touch someone else's post, and only UUID-shaped ids are accepted because the "show the rest" query interpolates them into a PostgREST `not.in.(…)` filter string.
- **`ProfilePage` + `Person` JSON-LD** (`profilePageLd`, deferred back in B8), with the Person carrying a stable `@id` of `<page-url>#person`. `articleLd` now takes `authorName`/`authorUrl` and stamps that same `@id` on every DB post's author, so a writer resolves as one entity across the site instead of a repeated name string; profile links become `sameAs`. MDX posts pass neither and keep the site-owner default they have always emitted. 8 new cases in `lib/json-ld.test.ts`, 12 in a new `lib/author-profile.test.ts`.

### Fixed
- **`npm run lint` was dead repo-wide since the Cloudflare migration.** `eslint.config.mjs` `globalIgnores` never gained `.open-next/**`, and because the script is a bare `eslint` it lints the whole working directory: `.open-next` is **332 MB across 3,112 JS files**, so the run died with `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit`, still fatal at `--max-old-space-size=8192`. Added `.open-next/**` and `.wrangler/**` alongside the existing `.next/**` entry. `npm run lint` now exits 0 (0 errors, 2 pre-existing `no-unused-vars` warnings in `lib/content-fs.ts` that were simply unreachable while the run crashed).

### Changed
- **Bylines link to the author, on the post page and on the `/blog` cards.** `PostAuthor` gains an optional `href`, so the link is single-sourced through `PostHeader` and DraftEditor's view mode inherits it. The `/blog` card meta row moved OUT of the card's `<Link>` — an `<a>` inside an `<a>` is invalid HTML — and cards show a byline only where a profile exists, which is also what keeps legacy MDX posts looking exactly as they did.
- **`app/(app)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` now uses `PostHeader`** instead of a byte-for-byte copy of its markup. The component's own header comment already claimed this path as one of its two consumers; the duplicate had drifted in, and the byline link had to be identical in both places.
- **`author.display_name` outranks Clerk on Paddock surfaces.** Clerk was authoritative for the rendered byline, which was right while the row was operator-seeded and wrong the moment the author types a name into our own form. Clerk now supplies the avatar, and the name only as the fallback for a writer with no profile row. `resolveBlogAuthor` moved out of the blog page into `lib/author-identity.ts` (`resolveAuthorIdentity`) so the profile page and the byline that links to it cannot disagree; the KV key is unchanged (`paddock:blog-author:<id>`) so warm entries keep serving.
- Sitemap gains `/authors` plus one URL per profile, and only when at least one profile exists — an empty index is a thin page we would be advertising. `listAuthors` is fail-soft, so an unreachable DB drops those entries instead of failing the whole sitemap.

## 0.245.2 — 2026-07-31

### Fixed
- **The cancelled Bahrain Grand Prix is back, in October, in a different country.** `content/series/f1/rounds.json` held 22 rounds and jumped Azerbaijan (24 Sep) straight to Singapore (9 Oct), while formula1.com lists **23**. The gap was not an oversight: the file's own `cancelledRounds` carried Bahrain, dropped from round 4 (10-12 April) over the Middle East conflict, with `rescheduleStatus: "Under discussion for the 2-4 October weekend, not yet officially confirmed by F1/FIA"`. That confirmation now exists — F1 and the FIA state "Malaysia will host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit from October 2-4 2026" (subject to final agreements and WMSC sign-off), so the round is restored at **16**, renumbering Singapore→17 through Abu Dhabi→23, and its `cancelledRounds` entry removed — leaving it there would have the cancellation banner announce Bahrain as called off while round 16 showed it scheduled. `previousStartDate`/`previousEndDate`/`rescheduleNote` carry the provenance, which drives "Rescheduled from 10-12 Apr · relocated to Sepang, Malaysia" in `WeekendBlock` and `eventStatus: EventRescheduled` in the SportsEvent markup. Session overrides were unaffected: `lib/sessions-overrides.ts` matches on `matchDate` with a ±2 day window, not on round numbers. The Saudi Arabian Grand Prix stays cancelled.
- **The trap:** the event is named after one country and held in another, and the F1 feed publishes `LOCATION: ""` for all five of its sessions (all at `T000000Z`, dates only). Circuit resolution therefore fell back to the round name, matched the `"Bahrain Grand Prix"` alias, and would have rendered the race with **Sakhir's weather, map, coordinates and a timezone three hours out**. New optional `venue` on `SeriesRoundEntry` (`lib/types.ts`) plus `venueCandidates()` (`lib/circuits.ts`), consumed by both weekend pages for the map and the SportsEvent geo lookup. The venue is used **ALONE**, not as one candidate among several, because `matchCircuitEntry` flattens every alias, sorts longest-first and returns the first alias found in ANY candidate — so candidate order carries no priority and the wrong circuit could win on string length. `content/circuits.json` already had Sepang (`lat 2.7606, lon 101.7375`, `MY`), so weather and structured data are correct; no layout exists for it, so the track map is absent for that weekend rather than showing Bahrain's.
- **WEC 2026's last two rounds were wrong in both directions.** Ours had Qatar 1812 km (22-24 Oct) and Bahrain 8h (5-7 Nov). fiawec.com and the live Google-calendar ICS the app consumes **both** list **6 Hours of Barcelona (18 Oct)** and **6 Hours of Monza (8 Nov)**, with **zero** Qatar or Bahrain events in the feed. Rounds 7 and 8 replaced, weekend windows Fri-Sun per the file's own convention for European rounds with the race on the final day (18 Oct and 8 Nov both probed as Sundays). Six orphaned session-override blocks for Lusail and Sakhir removed — not cosmetic: the Sakhir blocks sat on 5-7 Nov and Monza's weekend is 6-8 Nov, so the ±2 day override window would have injected Bahrain sessions into the Monza weekend.
- 11 new tests (`lib/circuits.test.ts`, `lib/rounds-calendar.test.ts`) covering the venue-alone rule, the Sepang resolution, the Bahrain-without-venue fallback that documents why the rule exists, and data-integrity guards on both calendars.

### Notes
- Barcelona and Monza carry **no session timetables yet** — the WEC feed publishes one event per round, and no official timetable has been released. They will show the race only until itineraries publish and a curated override can carry real times. Times were deliberately not projected from a template: that is what produced the Hungary drift corrected in 0.234.2.
- Only F1 and WEC were checked. Two of two were stale, so the other 13 series are unverified.
## 0.245.1 — 2026-07-28

### Added
- **A third preview Worker, `motorsport-panagiotis` on `panagiotis.paddock-tracker.com`**, fed by the `testing-panagiotis` branch. Same shape as the paris worker: no `triggers` block (crons must fire exactly once, on prod — a fourth worker firing them would quadruple-send pushes and re-publish posts against the same prod data), its own `panagiotis-cache` R2 prefix so ISR entries cannot collide, `WORKER_SELF_REFERENCE` pointing at itself, `DATA_SOURCE=db`. No DNS record needed: the zone's wildcard `*.paddock-tracker.com` A records already resolve any subdomain, and the `routes` entry is what makes the Worker answer.
- **`scripts/sync-worker-secrets.mts`** (`npm run secrets:sync -- <paris|panagiotis|testing>`) — bulk-sets the 10-key preview secret set on a preview Worker, reading `.env.production.local` through `tsx --env-file` so Node strips the quotes those values carry. Prints names and lengths, never values; writes the payload to a 0600 temp file and removes it in a `finally` so a failure cannot leave secrets on disk. Refuses production outright, because the env file holds 10 of prod's 23 and a "sync" there would be a partial overwrite dressed as a full one. Guards against a value arriving still-quoted, which is the failure that fed Supabase `"https://…"` and broke every warm-cron write for ~20 hours while reporting success.

### Removed
- **Every Vercel package is out of the tree.** `@vercel/analytics` and `@vercel/speed-insights` only report from Vercel-hosted deployments, so since the migration they shipped bytes and collected nothing (the components had already gone — `docs/HANDOFF.md:77` records it — but the dependencies were left declared). `@vercel/kv` is replaced by `@upstash/redis` behind a new `lib/kv.ts`: it was an 80-line subclass of that same client, its only dependency, reading the same `KV_REST_API_*` credentials, so this is a library change and **not** a data migration — same store, same keys, nothing moved. The shim reproduces two options that are **not** upstream defaults, and getting either wrong would have been silent: `cache: 'default'` (`@upstash/redis` defaults to `no-store`) and `enableAutoPipelining: true` (off upstream, and leaving it off would multiply round trips to a store already 180ms from the Athens colo). Construction stays lazy behind a Proxy with `then`/`parse` passed through, because most of the test suite imports these modules with no KV env present and a module-level `new Redis(...)` would throw at import. The four `*ScanIterator` helpers are dropped, verified unused. 14 source importers and 8 test files repointed; `lib/kv.ts` is now the single seam for any future move off Upstash, which stays a separate project because `paddock:push:*`, `paddock:user:*` and `paddock:consent:*` are not regenerable.
  Parity was proven against the live store before repointing anything, both clients side by side, read-only: a real cached object came back deep-equal, `scan` returned the same cursor type and shape, a missing key gave `null` in both, `mget` matched, and a real hash `hgetall` matched. Then a full round trip through `lib/results-cache` with the shim: write, read deep-equal, `del` → 1, subsequent read `null`. Worth recording for the next person who probes SCAN: a `MATCH`-filtered scan can return an empty batch on cursor 0 even when matching keys exist, because it filters per batch — the first parity attempt fell for that and compared `null` to `null`.

### Notes
- **Cloudflare Secrets Store was evaluated and rejected**, with the reasoning recorded in the script's header so nobody re-opens it blind: its bindings are async-only (`await env.X.get()`), while this codebase — and the Clerk and Supabase SDKs inside it — read `process.env.*` synchronously. Adopting it would require an async hydration shim in `worker.ts` populating `process.env` before any SDK initialises, on every cold start, whose failure mode is silent: everything reads as unconfigured and the fail-soft layers serve empty pages. It is also open beta and cannot serve production secrets to local dev. Not worth it to avoid one command.

## 0.245.0 — 2026-07-28

### Added
- **A preview Worker per developer, restoring the branch → URL → PR → prod shape the Vercel workflow had.** `wrangler.paris.jsonc` adds `motorsport-paris` on `paris.paddock-tracker.com`, fed by the `testing-paris` branch, alongside the existing `motorsport-testing` on `testing.paddock-tracker.com` fed by `testing`. Cloudflare cannot do this the way Vercel did: **Preview URLs are not generated for Workers that implement a Durable Object** (their docs), and `worker.ts:21` exports three, so a live URL requires a real Worker and one Worker serves one deployment — two devs pushing to a shared preview would silently overwrite each other. Verified live: version `b623abde`, `/` and `/blog` and `/authors/paris-paraskevas` all 200 with `x-nextjs-cache: HIT` at 0.42-0.50s, 987 cache entries populated, and `pk_live_` keys in the HTML (which is what makes sign-in work there and impossible on localhost, since a Clerk production instance binds its session cookie to the app domain).
- **No DNS record was required.** The zone carries wildcard `*.paddock-tracker.com` A records, proxied — which is also why `testing` has always worked without a record of its own. Corollary worth knowing: a subdomain with **no** Worker route falls through that wildcard to the origin IPs, which still point at **Vercel**.
- Scripts: `deploy:paris` (build + deploy + populate), `deploy:cf:paris` (the Workers Builds counterpart), `cf:populate:paris`, and `deploy:cf` — the production counterpart of `deploy:cf:testing`, for Workers Builds to run on `main`. Its populate is deliberately **fatal** where testing's is swallowed: prod traffic does re-warm the R2 cache, but a silent cold cache is what 0.241.0 existed to fix, so the build should go red and say so.

### Changed
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md` rewritten where it had become false.** It still told contributors "Vercel auto-creates a preview deploy; the URL lands as a PR comment", and pointed them at a `.env.example` that does not exist. Now documents the three branch/worker/URL tiers, what previews share with prod (the same Supabase, KV and R2 bucket — so app mutations on a preview write to **prod data**), what they deliberately cannot do (no `RESEND_API_KEY`, no `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`, no analytics keys, no cron triggers), the cherry-pick-from-workshop ritual, the `merge origin/main -X theirs` sync, and where every secret lives plus the three traps that have each cost a session.
- Preview secrets mirror testing's **10**, not prod's 23, so a preview cannot email the operator, push to real subscribers, or pollute analytics.

## 0.243.0 — 2026-07-27

### Performance
- **`/api/just-missed` + five `/api/home/*` routes moved to ISR — the `s-maxage` CDN contract died in the migration.** These routes were designed as "cacheable Ajax": `force-dynamic` + `Cache-Control: s-maxage` so the fan-out "runs at most once per window". That header contract was **Vercel's edge cache**; Cloudflare never caches Worker responses on headers alone (verified: no `cf-cache-status`/`x-nextjs-cache` on repeat prod hits), so since the migration every visitor re-ran every fan-out — just-missed measured 1.2s/hit on prod and 6-8s on the cron-less testing worker. Converted to `force-static` + `revalidate` (the `app/api/search` pattern, confirmed against the installed Next 16 route-handler docs), each keeping the exact staleness its own `s-maxage` declared: just-missed 300, spotlight 900, from-the-blog 300, upgrades 3600, latest-decoded 600, threads 120. Verified: just-missed 6-8s → **0.13s** `x-nextjs-cache: HIT` on testing, 1.2s → 0.29s on prod. NOT converted, each for cause: `bets` + `social` (user-shaped), `standings` + `movers` (read `?series=` — a static handler cannot use the request).

### Notes
- Testing worker redeployed with contributor commits after the `origin/testing` divergence was found and merged (the local branch had grown from a stale local-only commit; `merge-base --is-ancestor` now verified loudly for both sides). `origin/testing` pushed at the operator's request. The four warm-live-data repo secrets were set by the operator; the scheduled refresh activates when this branch reaches `main`.

The subdomain's DNS was already Cloudflare-proxied (it 402'd at dead Vercel), so the route alone intercepts it. ## 0.241.0 — 2026-07-27

### Added
- **A real ISR page cache on the Worker (R2 + DO queue + regional cache).** `open-next.config.ts` had been passing `defineCloudflareConfig({})`, leaving `incrementalCache` at the adapter's `"dummy"` default — no page cache at all, so every request re-rendered (`x-nextjs-cache: MISS` on every hit, measured on prod). Now: `r2IncrementalCache` (bucket `paddock-inc-cache`, `eeur` location hint) wrapped in `withRegionalCache(…, { mode: 'long-lived' })`, plus the Durable Object queue. **The queue is required, not optional**: the default `"dummy"` queue THROWS `FatalError("Dummy queue is not implemented")` from `queue.send`, which is exactly what a stale ISR page calls to schedule its background revalidation — a real cache without a queue would fail on every stale page. `wrangler.jsonc` gains the R2 binding, the `NEXT_CACHE_DO_QUEUE` DO binding + `v1` SQLite migration, and the `WORKER_SELF_REFERENCE` service binding the DO needs to call back in. Result on prod: `x-nextjs-cache: HIT`, `/series/f1/standings` **9.34s → 0.12s**, `/series/motogp/results` 1.63s → 0.26s, `/calendar` 0.16s, `/drivers/<slug>` 0.14s.
- **Cost control, sized against the published limits** (R2 free tier = 10 GB / 1M Class A / 10M Class B, no egress — developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing, checked 2026-07-27). Storage is a non-issue (the whole build cache is 134 MB). The regional cache absorbs reads before they reach R2 (per opennext.js.org/cloudflare/caching). `series/[slug]/[tab]` moves `revalidate` 300 → **1200** to match the 20-minute warm cron that is now the only thing that changes what those tabs render — at 300s each data change cost four R2 writes instead of one. Sibling routes stay at 300s because they carry live session state. Writes only occur when a stale page is actually requested, so Class A cannot exceed ISR page requests; deploy-time population is 562 writes (0.06% of the tier), and Durable Objects are inside the Workers Paid allowance with no charge while idle.

### Fixed
- **F1 session classifications rendered `#1` / `#3` instead of driver names.** Three compounding defects, all evidenced: (1) `fetchJson` in `lib/results/openf1.ts` called raw `fetch` — bypassing both the rate limiter and `fetchUpstream`, so no pacing, no timeout, no logging, and a 429 silently became `null`; (2) the paced client (`lib/openf1/client.ts`) enforced only 3 req/s while OpenF1's free tier documents **3 req/s AND 30 req/min** (openf1.org, checked 2026-07-27) — 3/s sustained is 180/min, six times over; (3) the half-failed result was then persisted for its 7-day TTL. On a weekend session page, which fans out to several OpenF1 endpoints at once, `/session_result` succeeded while its parallel `/drivers` was throttled to `[]`, and that got frozen in. Fixes: the old client now routes through the paced one; the limiter enforces both buckets; `fetchSessionClassification` falls back to the curated F1 grid (`content/series/f1/drivers.json` carries each car number) when `/drivers` is empty; and new `hasResolvedDrivers` gates both cache-write sites (`weekend/[round]/[session]` page + the warm-sessions cron, which gains a `no-driver-names` outcome) so a nameless classification can never be written again. 4 new tests.
- **Repaired the two poisoned cache entries in place.** A scan of all 227 `paddock:session-class:*` keys found exactly 2 bad ones — `f1:2026:11:qualifying` and `f1:2026:11:race` — consistent with both having been warmed at session end, inside OpenF1's paid live window. Recomputed from a clean IP and overwritten (not deleted): the Hungary race now reads Norris / Verstappen / Antonelli with teams. The other 225 were healthy.

### Notes
- The deploy-time R2 cache-population step fails against the bucket ("Failed to send request to R2 worker: fetch failed" after 15 retries) even though direct `wrangler r2 object put`/`get` round-trips fine, so deploys currently run with population skipped (`OPEN_NEXT_DEPLOY=true wrangler deploy`) and the cache fills lazily on first request per page. Worth chasing, not blocking.
- `wrangler deploy` inside an OpenNext project **delegates to `opennextjs-cloudflare deploy`** by design (`dist/cli/commands/deploy.js` sets `OPEN_NEXT_DEPLOY=true` to break the recursion) — which is why a plain `wrangler deploy` ran the cache-population step.

## 0.240.0 — 2026-07-27

### Added
- **DB-as-single-source-of-truth for standings + results (`DATA_SOURCE=db`).** Root cause of the post-Cloudflare "data is non-deterministically wrong": the render path still called the community APIs on every request, and a Cloudflare colo that *wasn't* rate-limited returned a PARTIAL payload which then overwrote the good last-good cache. Measured on prod before the fix: three consecutive fetches of `/series/f1/standings` returned three different byte lengths, and the season-trend payload stopped at **round 5 (Canada)** while the season was at round 11. Compounding it, `open-next.config.ts` passes `defineCloudflareConfig({})` and the adapter defaults `incrementalCache` to `"dummy"` (`node_modules/@opennextjs/cloudflare/dist/api/config.js:45`) — so there is NO ISR cache on the Worker at all (`x-nextjs-cache: MISS` on every hit) and *every* request re-rendered and re-fetched. Fix: `isDbReadOnly()` in `lib/source-snapshot.ts` (env `DATA_SOURCE=db`, set as a Worker var in `wrangler.jsonc`) makes both cache wrappers — `withSourceSnapshot` and `withF1LastGood` (`lib/f1-cache.ts`) — pure READERS: a present snapshot is returned and the upstream fetch never runs; an unseeded slot still falls through to the fetcher (so a not-yet-warmed surface isn't blank) but the result is NEVER persisted. `scripts/warm-live-data.mts`, run from clean IPs by `.github/workflows/warm-live-data.yml`, is the only writer.
- **A durable DB slot for every data surface.** DB mode is only as good as what the DB holds, and most fetchers had nothing durable behind them: standings for **motogp / wsbk / imsa** had no snapshot wrapper at all; results for **f2 / f3 (via `fom-api`) / dtm / wec / wsbk** had only a 3-hour KV window; results for **motogp / wrc / formula-e / indycar / nascar-cup / gt-world / imsa / nls** had no cache whatsoever. All are now wrapped at their public export boundary (live parser renamed `fetchX…Live`, public name + signature unchanged, so no call site moved). New `withRaceResultsSnapshot` + `reviveRaceDates` in `lib/source-snapshot.ts` carry the `RaceResult[]` case, whose `date` field jsonb round-trips to an ISO string; WEC (`dateStart`/`dateEnd`), IMSA (`date`) and the FOM bundle rehydrate in their own modules. `fetchDTMSeasonChartData` needs no wrapper (it derives from the already-snapshotted DTM standings), and `fetchWsbkLastRace` inherits the wrapper by reading through `fetchWsbkSeasonResults`.
- **`scripts/warm-live-data.mts` now covers every slot, not just the health registries.** The two registries reach 13 standings + 8 results; the new `EXTRA_SURFACES` pass adds F1 sprints + last-race, the WRC chart series, and results for **indycar (with curated drivers), dtm, nascar-cup, nls, gt-world, imsa, wec** — each called with the SAME arguments the page passes, because a snapshot key is per-surface, not per-argument (IndyCar's curated-driver name normalisation is the live example: the health registry calls it with `{}`). The script now also aborts if `SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are missing (the tier the site actually reads) or if `DATA_SOURCE=db` leaked into the runner env (which would turn the writer into a reader and the run into a silent no-op), and its two pre-existing `'DOWN'` status comparisons — a value `HealthStatus` never carries, so the summary line always claimed success — now test `OK`/`LOW`.
- Worker route for **`dev.paddock-tracker.com`** (`wrangler.jsonc`). Its DNS record is already proxied through Cloudflare (verified: `Server: cloudflare` + `CF-RAY`, forwarding to the disabled Vercel project → 402), so the route alone intercepts it; no DNS change.

### Performance
- **Snapshot-first reads in DB mode.** Latency measured from the Athens colo (`CF-RAY … -ATH`) 2026-07-27: TCP RTT to Supabase **17ms** (44ms with TLS), to the Upstash KV store **180ms** (236ms with TLS) — the KV database is not in an EU region. Outside DB mode KV is correctly the hot tier (per-render read-through); inside it both tiers hold the identical payload from one warm run, so `withF1LastGood` now reads the near tier first. Separately, the reason the site felt slow again: with the request path still calling upstream and no ISR cache, a hanging source is paid by every visitor — `/series/f1/standings` measured **9.34s TTFB** on prod while `api.jolpi.ca` was timing out (30s, no response, from a clean residential IP too), against 0.24s for the static `/privacy`. DB mode removes that fetch from the render path entirely.
- Known, NOT addressed here: the Worker has no incremental cache (`incrementalCache` defaults to `"dummy"`), so every request re-renders; and the KV store's region means user-preference / push-subscription reads still cross an ocean. Both need an infra decision — an R2 bucket for the ISR cache, and a KV region move that is a real data migration (`paddock:push:*`, `paddock:user:*`, `paddock:followed*`, `paddock:consent:*`, `paddock:contact:*` are not regenerable).

### Fixed
- **`worker.ts` had no default export** — only the named Durable Object re-exports, which Workers rejects as "no registered event handlers". The deployed artifact predated the omission, so the live site was fine but the tree could not be redeployed. Restored `export default workerHandler` with a comment naming the failure mode.
- **DTM results were showing one event, mislabelled.** `harvestPicker` selected `a.msnt-select__option--event`, but motorsport.com dropped the `--event` modifier (verified 2026-07-27: 0 matches out of 2 picker links), so event discovery returned nothing and the feed fell back to the single event the landing URL redirects to — tagged R1 and stamped with a *different* event's date (Oschersleben as "R1, 2026-03-22", which is Red Bull Ring's weekend). Now matches both class forms and lets `eventSlugFromUrl` reject non-event links. Live: 2 races → 6, correctly numbered R1 Red Bull Ring / R2 Zandvoort / R3 Oschersleben. Upstream still publishes only 3 of the 5 completed rounds — a source-coverage gap, not a parser one.
- **NASCAR Cup results were silently EMPTY.** `parseSeasonRaceLinks` anchored on `a[href^="/wiki/2026_"]`, but Wikipedia now serves those hrefs ABSOLUTE (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Daytona_500`) — verified live 2026-07-27: 125 candidate rows, 0 matched. Same break that killed the WRC parser in 0.229.13. Switched to `href*=` plus a local `normalizeWikiHref` (relative / protocol-relative / absolute), mirroring `lib/results/wrc.ts`. Live parse recovered 22 races / 832 classification rows.

### Changed
- Deleted the 13 GitHub Actions cron workflows superseded by the in-Worker Cron Triggers (`award-prizes`, `betting-notify`, `grant-credits`, `health`, `news`, `notify`, `open-markets`, `publish-posts`, `race-week`, `recheck-results`, `settle-markets`, `warm-results`, `warm-sessions`). `warm-live-data.yml` stays — it is now load-bearing: GitHub's clean IPs are the only ones that can reach the data APIs.
- Tests: 7 new cases pinning DB-mode behaviour (`lib/source-snapshot.test.ts`, `lib/f1-cache.test.ts`) — snapshot served without invoking the fetcher, no write on the miss path so a partial upstream payload can never overwrite the DB, KV→snapshot fallback still fetch-free, and an unseeded slot degrading to a fetch-but-don't-write. Suite 931 → 938.

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vitest run` 98 files / 938 tests pass.
- Seeded prod from a clean IP: 13/13 standings + 8/8 results + 10/10 extra surfaces; `source_snapshot` shows every `standings:*` / `results:*` key written (39 rows).
- Prod `/api/cron/health` returns all 13 standings + 8 results OK (the 503 is the `sessions` dimension flagging WRC as thin — a curation gap, not a data-layer break).
- Not done: notify fail-quiet was unnecessary — prod `/api/push/status` reports `vapidConfigured: true` and `/api/cron/notify` returns `200 {"ok":true,"message":"nothing to send"}`, so the handoff's "notify 500s every minute" is stale.

Vibrant fills moved to `bg/from/fill/stroke-brand-fill|tint-fill` via codemod — 100 call sites across 62 files; the 217 text/border/ring usages needed no edits and can't regress into illegibility. Pages injecting a series tint now set both `--tint` and `--tint-fill` (8 sites). shadcn bridge: `--primary`/`--chart-1`/`--sidebar-primary` → `var(--tint-fill)`.
- **Inline series/team colours as text** now route through `seriesInk()` — 23 `style={{ color: X }}` sites (HomeContent ×14, news/drivers/teams/Champions, SectorBars/GhostLapReplay/GhostLap3D team-colour deltas) + 8 shorthand `style={{ color }}` sites (weekend/compare/analysis/session heroes' series-coloured full stops, WeekendNewsClient labels). ### Fixed

(1) `public/manifest.json` had no `scope` (start_url `/app`), so navigations to `/blog/*` (and any path outside `/app`) could be treated as out-of-scope and open in an external in-app browser — added `"scope": "/"` so the whole origin stays inside the installed app. (2) `components/blog/PostModeration.tsx` opened the draft-preview link with `target="_blank"`, which a standalone PWA renders as a Custom Tab — dropped it (and the "opens in a new tab" affordance) so previewing a draft navigates in-app; back returns to the queue.

## 0.232.0 — 2026-07-23

### Added
- **Like / dislike reactions on blog posts.** End-of-post widget `components/blog/BlogReactions.tsx` + flat API `app/api/blog/reactions/route.ts` (GET / POST / DELETE) + data layer `lib/blog-reactions.ts` + migration `supabase/migrations/20260723120000_post_reaction.sql`. One reaction per identity per post, keyed by post **slug** (immutable, and covers legacy MDX posts): signed-in readers dedup by Clerk `user_id`, anonymous readers by a **salted IP hash** — HMAC-SHA256 keyed on `CRON_SECRET`, computed in the route, so the raw IP is never stored (no PII in the table). Storing `user_id` leaves room for a future suggested-posts list built from likes. Partial unique indexes enforce the dedup; the API does select-then-insert/update because Postgres can't infer a partial index from a plain `ON CONFLICT`. Per-IP rate limit via `allowRequest` (fail-open, not cost-bearing). RLS-on / no-policies / service_role-only. Fail-soft: the widget shows zeros if Supabase or the table is unavailable. **The prod migration must be applied before counts persist.**

## 0.230.2 — 2026-07-21

### Fixed
- Greek lowercase omega (ω, U+03C9) rendered as a capital Ω in blog prose and anywhere body text is Greek. Root cause: GeistSans (the body face, `geist/font/sans`) ships a malformed glyph for U+03C9 — a real-but-wrong glyph, so the browser never fell back to a correct one (other Greek letters are fine; only ω). Fix in `app/globals.css`: a `unicode-range` `@font-face` (`GreekFallback`, Greek U+0370–03FF + Greek-Extended U+1F00–1FFF → `local()` system faces) placed ahead of the Geist stack on `body`, so Greek codepoints resolve to a correct system glyph while Latin/numerals stay Geist untouched. `font-mono`/`font-display` set their own family and are unaffected (Saira already falls back correctly for Greek). Reproduced + verified in Chrome: ω resolves to the system lowercase glyph, Latin advance widths unchanged. Unblocks Greek-language posts.

## 0.230.1 — 2026-07-21

### Added
- Lap-by-lap analysis blog variant — grounding engine + playbook (no prod runtime). New `scripts/lapstory-context.mts` (F1-only) resolves a round's OpenF1 race session (`fetchOpenF1WeekendSessions` date-overlap + a `session_name === 'Race'` pick) and emits a deterministic race-chronology pack: authoritative tier (final classification + DNFs with stop-lap via `fetchSessionClassification`, tyre stints, pit laps/durations, safety-car/VSC/red-flag neutralisations, penalties) plus the full-field OpenF1 `overtakes` feed, lap-anchored via a lap clock (earliest `date_start` per lap) and flagged `likelyPitCycle` (either driver pitted ±1 lap) so pit-cycling isn't written as on-track passes. Self-contained plain-fetch OpenF1 (no paced client / KV) with retry-until-non-empty pacing (~600ms, 7 tries): the 3 req/s free tier was intermittently throttling `race_control`/`pit`/`laps` to `[]` and silently dropping the safety cars/penalties — now deterministic across runs, with a loud guard if a must-be-populated dataset is still empty. Companion playbook `docs/content-authoring/lapstory-post-playbook.md` (analyst voice; RULE #1 fact-tiering: authoritative verbatim, decisive passes cross-checked vs primary reports, midfield passes attributed to OpenF1 timing, mandatory OpenF1 attribution line). First output (Belgian GP 2026 lap-by-lap) created as a prod DB draft via the standard SOP. Automation (post-race grounding cron + auto-draft) is a preview-gated follow-up riding the queued weekend-post cadence trigger, not shipped here. Verified: grounding deterministic across 3 runs for Spa (45 laps, 3 DNFs, 28 stops, 6 neutralisations, 93 on-track overtakes); `tsc` clean; `next build` green.

## 0.230.0 — 2026-07-21

### Added
- Blog cover images + branded share cards. Root cause of the "my profile pic shows when I share a post" report: `app/(app)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` emitted `og:image` only when a post had a `hero_image` (which nothing could set post-creation), so share scrapers fell back to the only prominent `<img>` on the page — the Clerk byline avatar. Fix in three parts: **(1) editable cover** — `PostContentPatch.heroImage` in `lib/blog.ts` (`normalizeHeroImage`: https:// or root-relative only, null/blank clears; shared with `createDraft`), accepted by PATCH `/api/blog/[id]`, and a "Cover image URL" field + preview in `DraftEditor` (the 2026-07-03 spec's hero-immutability deliberately reversed); **(2) cover rendered on the post** — new `PostHero` in `components/blog/PostHeader.tsx`, used by the public page + DraftEditor view mode (a set hero previously fed metadata only and never displayed); **(3) share card** — new `app/(app)/blog/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx` (`ImageResponse`): the series-tinted branded card in the weekend-card visual language for EVERY post, generic card for drafts (no leak through the unauthenticated image route). A full-bleed-photo card variant was built and dropped on operator review — cover quality varies, the branded card is sharp every time; covers are on-page only. The page's `openGraph.images` was removed — file-based metadata overrides `generateMetadata` (Next 16 docs), so the file owns `og:image` unconditionally. Sourcing SOP (Commons/Flickr-CC with credit, Unsplash/Pexels, never agencies) baked into the `blog-authoring` skill §4 + the weekend-post playbook. Tests: 4 new `updatePostContent` hero cases (15 total across blog suites); OG card + on-page hero browser-verified on dev.

## 0.229.15 — 2026-07-20

### Added
- Weekend-schedule health monitor (`lib/sessions-health.ts` + `scripts/health-sessions.mts`; `npm run health:sessions`, folded into `npm run health` and `/api/cron/health`). The standings/results monitors only count rows, so a broken per-round timetable stayed invisible — GT World's Misano weekend silently rendered only "Free Practice 2" (its `sessions.json` override dropped the real races) while standings stayed green. The new check groups each series into weekends and flags any COMPLETED round whose session count is anomalously low vs that series' own median (floor = median × 0.5), excluding stray `round < 1` buckets; a 0-session round grades EMPTY. Self-calibrating — no per-series floors, no fragile race-name detection — so single-session-per-round feeds (NASCAR, IndyCar ovals) don't false-trip while a 1-session weekend in a 5–6-session series does. Contributes to the cron's `down` count (503) so incomplete schedules alert like a down source. Known v1 gap: it counts sessions, so it does not yet catch a round with the right count but wrong days/times (needs official-timetable cross-referencing). First run surfaced the curation gap-list: `gt-world` (R4 Spa, R5 Misano), `dtm` (R4 Norisring), `wrc` (R4 Croatia), `indycar` (R3/R8/R10/R11 — road/street rounds missing practice+qualifying). Verified: `tsc` clean; `sessions-health.test.ts` 6/6; `npm run health:sessions` → 15 series, 4 flagged.

## 0.229.14 — 2026-07-20

### Fixed
- F2 + F3 results feeds restored (both `EMPTY` in `npm run health:results` for ~1 week). The FIA rebuilt fiaformula2.com / fiaformula3.com onto a Next.js App-Router frontend: `/Standings/Driver` + `/Results?raceid=N` now redirect to `/en/standings/2026/drivers` + `/en/racing/2026/<venue>`, which carry no `#__NEXT_DATA__` (data streams via `__next_f` RSC) and server-render only the feature race — sprint/qualifying/practice load client-side — so `extractNextData` in `lib/results/f2.ts`+`f3.ts` was dead at the root. Rewritten onto the FOM JSON API (`api.formula1.com/v2/core-fom-results`) the sites' own client calls, via a new shared client `lib/results/fom-api.ts`: one `driver-standings-breakdown` call for the meeting manifest + canonical per-round `[SR,FR]` points, then a per-completed-round `race`/`qualifying`/`practice` fan-out (gated on rounds with non-null points, capped concurrency, fail-soft). `f2.ts`/`f3.ts` are now thin adapters preserving their public signatures (`fetchF2SeasonResults` → `{feature,sprint,qualifying,practice}`; `fetchF3SeasonResults` → `RaceResult[]`; `fetchF3SessionResults` → `{qualifying,practice}`). Points are sourced from the standings breakdown, NOT the per-session `racePoints` field (which omits pole/fastest-lap bonuses) — validated: summed `[SR,FR]` reconciles to `championshipPoints` for all 22 F2 + 33 F3 drivers, both via a standalone probe and the live implementation. Championship round = manifest meeting index+1 (the API's only round number is the F1 GP number, which differs — F2/F3 skip GPs; trusting it would misindex the points array). Corrected the stale `motorsport.com` source labels in `lib/results-health.ts` → `FOM API`. ⚠ Landmine: this depends on the public `apikey` embedded in each site's client bundle (per-brand; documented in `fom-api.ts`) — fail-soft to last-good KV cache if FOM rotates it. Verified: `npm run health:results` → F2 711 rows, F3 369 rows, all 8 sources green; `tsc` clean; 915 tests pass; live points reconciliation 22/22 F2 + 33/33 F3.

## 0.228.6 — 2026-07-14

### Fixed
- SportsEvent structured data now emits every field Google Search Console flagged as missing, on the weekend event AND on each per-session sub-event (`lib/json-ld.ts` `sportsEventLd`). Previously the recommended fields were emitted only on the top-level weekend event and only when the caller supplied them; every `subEvent` was a bare SportsEvent (name / startDate / endDate / url / location), so GSC flagged `description`, `image`, `performer`, `organizer` (+ `url`), `offers`, and `eventStatus` as missing on the sub-events, and the session page's own SportsEvent additionally lacked `address`, `description`, `performer`, and `offers`. Fields, and where each is sourced:
  - `organizer` always carries a `url` (series `officialSite`, else the on-site series hub `/series/<slug>`).
  - `performer` is always populated: the curated team roster as `SportsTeam[]` when available (`lib/series-content.ts` `loadCuratedDrivers`), else the series itself as a `SportsOrganization` (used by session pages, which pass no roster).
  - `offers` emits an `Offer` (url + `category: watch` + `availability: InStock`) from `series.meta.watch`. No price, since these are subscription/broadcast links whose cost is not tracked; skipped cleanly when a series has no watch link.
  - `eventStatus` adds `EventCancelled` (from `rounds.json` `cancelled`); the existing `EventRescheduled` (+ `previousStartDate`) and default `EventScheduled` are unchanged (0.227.1 not regressed).
  - `description` is always present (caller-supplied, else generated "Round N of the <season> <series> season."). The session page (`app/(app)/series/[slug]/weekend/[round]/[session]/page.tsx`) now resolves the circuit (`matchCircuitEntry`) + round meta too, so its event carries `location.address` (country) + geo and a session-specific description.
  - Each enrichment (description, image, location incl. address/geo, organizer, performer, offers, eventStatus) is copied onto every `subEvent` so each validates independently. Sub-events take `EventScheduled`/`EventCancelled` (no per-session `previousStartDate`, so never an unpaired `EventRescheduled`).
  - `image`: kept as the stable brand logo (`icons/icon-512.png`) and now emitted on sub-events too. The per-weekend OG image route was evaluated and rejected: Next serves it at a build-hashed path (`/…/opengraph-image-<hash>?<contenthash>`; the bare `/opengraph-image` returns HTML, verified on a running dev server), so hard-referencing it in structured data would break silently on any rebuild.
  - `location.address` stays country-only (no `addressLocality`): `content/circuits.json` carries no city field, so a locality would be fabricated.
  - Callers: weekend page (`app/(app)/series/[slug]/weekend/[round]/page.tsx`) now passes `watch` + `cancelled`; session page passes `description`, `watch`, `addressCountry`, `venue`, `geo`, `cancelled`. Coverage extended in `lib/json-ld.test.ts` (offers presence/skip, eventStatus cancelled/rescheduled, sub-event enrichment, performer + organizer.url fallbacks). Verified on a dev server against F1 (roster teams, F1 TV offer) and NASCAR (roster teams, nascar.com offer) weekend + session pages.

The dashboard moved out of the `(app)` route group (`app/(app)/admin/**` → `app/(admin)/admin/**`) into a NEW standalone root route group `app/(admin)/` with its own root `layout.tsx` (`<html>/<body>`, Geist + Saira fonts, `globals.css`, and a `ClerkProvider` mirroring the `(app)` group so auth still resolves). Route-group parens keep every URL unchanged (`/admin`, `/admin/traffic`, …). Because `(admin)` is a separate root, the console no longer inherits any `(app)` chrome. Dropped for admin: the site header/nav (`AppShell`), `Footer`, mobile `BottomBar`, `AssistantWidget`, `HeatmapTracker`, `CookieConsent`, `LaunchBanner`, the AdSense/GA `<Script>`s + consent shim, and Vercel `Analytics`/`SpeedInsights`. The admin gate (`requireAdmin()`) + amber nav rail stay in the nested `app/(admin)/admin/layout.tsx` (unchanged); the heatmap overlay and its `loadOverlayData` server action, all 7 routes, `components/admin/*`, `next.config.ts`, `proxy.ts`, and `lib/admin-guard.ts` are untouched. `robots: noindex` retained on the new root. Non-admins now hit the framework default 404 (bare, no chrome) instead of the `(app)` branded 404, acceptable for an operator-only surface.

### Fixed
- Admin panels no longer overflow / clip on the right at desktop or 390px mobile (operator-reported on `/admin/search` + `/admin/traffic`). Root cause: the big KPI numbers in `MiniStat`/`KpiTile` (`components/admin/AdminUI.tsx`) are unbreakable tokens; in narrow grid tracks they spilled past the tile and, because `html, body { overflow-x: clip }`, the spill was silently cut off rather than scrolled. Added `min-w-0` to both tile roots (so a tile can shrink to its grid track instead of forcing the row wider) and `truncate` on the numeric value (a hard guard against any spill); the `MiniStat` value is now `text-xl sm:text-2xl` so 6-7 digit figures fit the tightest mobile tiles. `SearchPanel`'s four KPIs changed from `sm:grid-cols-4` to a 2×2 `grid-cols-2` because the search route sits GSC + Bing side by side (`lg:grid-cols-2`), so four tiles were sharing a half-width column. Added `min-w-0` to the two search-route column wrappers. NOTE: in-browser confirmation is deferred to the operator, since the routes 404 for non-admins so the panels can't be rendered without an admin session.

## 0.228.0 — 2026-07-14

### Changed
- Admin console redesigned from one long anchor-scrolled page into a multi-page hub + seven gated routes under `app/(app)/admin/`. New `layout.tsx` owns the admin gate (`requireAdmin()`), an amber nav rail (`components/admin/AdminNav.tsx`, client, exact-match `usePathname` active state so `/admin` isn't lit on sub-routes), the `PAGE_WIDE` container + `lg:grid-cols-[200px_minmax(0,1fr)]` grid, `force-dynamic`, and `robots: noindex`. `page.tsx` is now an overview hub of `HubCard`s (one per destination route). Each sub-route — `traffic` (GA4 + a parked PageSpeed Insights panel), `search` (Search Console + Bing side by side), `behaviour` (heatmap overlay + hot/dead ranks), `users` (Clerk count + recent 25 with role badges + a sign-up-cadence sparkline), `submissions` (feeder intake), `tools` (links) — starts with `await requireAdmin()` + `force-dynamic` and fetches ONLY its own source(s), each fail-soft + env-gated with the connected / configured-but-empty / not-connected three-state. Rendering goes through a new server kit `components/admin/AdminUI.tsx`: AdminPageHeader, TelemetryPanel, KpiTile + inline-SVG Sparkline (no recharts), StatList + per-row DataBar, MiniStat, NotConnected/Unavailable, RankPanel/RankList, SubmissionRow/SubmissionStatusBadge, Traffic/Search/BingPanel, HubCard. The heatmap overlay (`components/admin/HeatmapOverlay.tsx`) is unchanged; its `loadOverlayData` server action was relocated verbatim into `behaviour/page.tsx` (keeping the `isAdmin(await currentUser())` re-check). The hub's KPI glances use only our own infra (heatmap click totals + Clerk `getCount`), so landing on the hub never doubles Google/Bing quota — each sub-page fetches its own source on demand.
- `requireAdmin()` lives in a new server-only module `lib/admin-guard.ts` (with an explicit `import 'server-only'`), NOT beside `isAdmin` in `lib/threads.ts` as first planned. Root cause: `threads.ts` is pulled into a client bundle by `ThreadComposer` (which imports its `TITLE_MAX`/`BODY_MAX`), and `@clerk/nextjs/server` transitively imports `server-only`; a static OR dynamic import of Clerk from `threads.ts` therefore fails the webpack client build (`'server-only' cannot be imported from a Client Component module`, trace: server-only ← @clerk/nextjs/server ← lib/threads.ts ← ThreadComposer.tsx). `threads.ts` is left unchanged; the guard imports `isAdmin` from it.

### Fixed
- Dead in-app link: the feeder-submission operator-notification email CTA (`lib/feeder.ts` `notifyNewSubmission`) pointed at `/admin#submissions`, an anchor that stopped existing when the admin sections became routes; now `/admin/submissions`.

## 0.222.0 — 2026-07-13

### Added
- **Heatmap Phase 2 — scroll-depth + rage/dead-click signals.** `components/HeatmapTracker.tsx` now also captures: per-pageview max SCROLL depth (rAF-throttled, scrollable pages only; emitted once on a terminal flush), RAGE clicks (≥3 clicks within 500 ms inside a 30 px box → one anchored 'rage' event), and DEAD clicks (a click with no interactive ancestor → 'dead' with a resolvable selector; interactive-but-untagged clicks stay 'click'). `lib/heatmap.ts`: `EventKind` / `KINDS` + `HeatmapEvent.value` extended; `sanitizeEvents` accepts `scroll` (needs a value, no anchor) + `rage`/`dead` (anchored); new reads `scrollStats` (reach curve via `bucketScrollDepths`) + `frustrationSignals` (rage/dead tallies via `aggregateFrustration`) + a combined `overlayData`.

Fed by the extended admin server action `loadOverlayData` (`app/(app)/admin/page.tsx`).

## 0.221.0 — 2026-07-13

### Added
- **Heatmap Phase 1 — a real visual click overlay on the actual page (operator: "see exactly where users clicked, on the page as it renders").** New `components/admin/HeatmapOverlay.tsx`: the `/admin` Behaviour section frames the real route in a same-origin iframe (`?hm=1`) and paints a best-practice density heatmap (radial-kernel accumulate → blue→red colour ramp) on a canvas over it, positioning each click by RE-RESOLVING its element in the live DOM (`[data-heatmap-id]` or a resolvable CSS path) and applying the stored in-element `relX/relY` — so hotspots land exactly on the real tabs/buttons at any breakpoint (per-breakpoint isolation; placed/total honesty count). Data via an admin-gated `loadClickPoints` server action + new `clickPoints()` / `bucketClickPoints()` in `lib/heatmap.ts` (reads the raw `heatmap_event` table, buckets per anchor onto a 1/50 grid). The Hot/Dead ranked lists stay below.
- **Capture upgrade** `components/HeatmapTracker.tsx`: every click (not just `data-heatmap-id` ones) now stores a re-resolvable rooted CSS path (`cssPath`, replacing the lossy 1-level `describe`) anchored to the nearest clickable element, plus `relX/relY` — so untagged clicks are positionable too. A `?hm=1` guard stops the tracker recording when a page is framed for inspection (no self-pollution).
- **Security header** `next.config.ts`: `X-Frame-Options` DENY→SAMEORIGIN + CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'`→`'self'` (report-only) so the admin can frame our own pages for the overlay; cross-origin (clickjacking) framing stays blocked.
- No migration (reuses existing `selector` / `rel_x` / `rel_y` columns). Verified: `next build` clean; 907/907 vitest (`bucketClickPoints` unit-tested); browser — synthetic points on `/app` painted exactly on the Calendar/Standings/Results/News chips (4/4 placed), correct density ramp, 0 console errors. Phases 2 (scroll/rage/dead) + 3 (segmentation/date-range) to follow.

## 0.213.0 — 2026-07-12

### Added
- **Sentry error monitoring + tracing (`@sentry/nextjs` v10, Next 16).** Wired across all three runtimes: `instrumentation-client.ts` (browser, + `onRouterTransitionStart`), `sentry.server.config.ts` + `sentry.edge.config.ts` loaded by `instrumentation.ts`'s `register()` (+ `onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError`), and `app/global-error.tsx` now also `captureException`s (kept its existing UI + `console.error`). `next.config.ts` is wrapped `withSentryConfig(withSerwist(nextConfig), …)` — Sentry outermost so its build plugin sees the final webpack config; the node-ical `serverExternalPackages` + `outputFileTracingIncludes` landmines are preserved untouched.
- **Scope: errors + tracing only** (`tracesSampleRate` 1.0 dev / 0.1 prod). Session Replay deliberately NOT enabled (records user sessions — a consent/privacy call the app's Consent Mode governs); `enableLogs` off (avoid PII from console capture); both are easy follow-ups. **No `tunnelRoute`** — the SDK posts straight to the ingest host, already covered by the CSP `connect-src https:`, so `proxy.ts` is untouched. DSN resolution: client reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`; server/edge read `SENTRY_DSN ?? NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, so one Vercel env var lights up all three. Source-map upload runs only when `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is set (build still passes without it). `.gitignore` extended for the SW `.map` siblings the source-map-enabled build now emits.
- Verified: tsc + eslint + `next build` clean (Sentry composes with Serwist; node-ical still traced). Browser smoke with the DSN set locally — client SDK initialised (`window.__SENTRY__` v10.65.0, carrier bound to our DSN) and a test error POSTed to `…ingest.de.sentry.io/…/envelope/` → **200** (events reach the project); DSN then removed from `.env.local`. **Operator: set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` in Vercel** (optionally `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` for readable prod stack traces) to enable on prod.

## 0.211.0 — 2026-07-12

### Added
- **Blog data-visual embeds — the shortcode→component pipeline (IDEAS B3), phase 1: pipeline + a live season-trend chart.** DB blog posts are plain markdown rendered to sanitised HTML (`renderMarkdown` → `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), so they couldn't host a live component. New `lib/blog-embeds.ts` `parseBodySegments` splits a body into ordered markdown / embed segments on a standalone `[[type key=value]]` line (a `[[` inside a paragraph or a fenced code block is left literal) **before** the markdown render — so the tokens never reach remark/rehype-sanitize: no sanitiser-schema change, no new XSS surface, and each markdown run renders exactly as before. `renderPostBody(body)` returns interleaved sanitised-HTML runs + embed specs plus a merged ToC, threading ONE dedup map through `injectHeadingIds` (new optional 2nd arg in `lib/toc.ts`) so heading ids stay unique and ToC anchors line up across an embed boundary.
- **`chart` embed** (`[[chart series=<slug>]]`) — `components/blog/embeds/ChartEmbed.tsx` renders the same `LazySeasonTrendChart` the Standings tab draws, from the same prod-proven `loadSnapshotSource` + `buildSeasonTrendData`. **Honours the locked chart-total invariant** (top of this file): only series whose feed carries championship-canonical per-round points (`pointsExact`) chart; the rest (WEC/IMSA/GTWC/NLS/ADAC, winners-only feeds) return null from the loader and fall back to a note, never a misleading line. `components/blog/embeds/BlogEmbed.tsx` dispatches by type (unknown → muted note); `components/blog/PostArticle.tsx` maps segments to sibling HTML `<div>`s + `not-prose` embed frames and is rendered on both the public `/blog/[slug]` path and `DraftEditor`'s preview (a server-rendered node passed into the client editor, so embeds show in preview too — `DraftEditor`'s `bodyHtml: string` prop became `bodyNode: ReactNode`).
- Every embed path is fail-soft (missing arg / unavailable data / thrown fetch / unknown type → a muted note; data-loading isolated from JSX per `react-hooks/error-boundaries`), so an embed can never throw out of the already-fail-soft post route. Parser unit-tested (`lib/blog-embeds.test.ts`, 10 cases: split/coalesce, quoted+unquoted args, whole-line-only match, fenced-code skip, adjacent embeds, ToC continuity across an embed). Suite 855→865. tsc + eslint + `next build` clean; browser-verified on a temp-mocked published post — the F1 chart rendered live 2026 data, WEC → honest "not available" note, unknown type → note, prose rhythm intact around embeds, 0 console errors. Standings embed + an authoring guide follow in the next PR.

## 0.202.0 — 2026-07-11

### Added
- **Click heatmap (admin behaviour panel).** A self-hosted, anonymous click heatmap so the operator can see which viewport regions of each page get clicks — and which dead zones to sell sponsorships in. **Capture:** `components/HeatmapTracker.tsx` (mounted app-wide) buckets each click into a 24×24 viewport grid for the current path, batches, and ships via `sendBeacon` on a timer / tab-hide / route change — **consent-gated** (`paddock:consent.analytics`) + honours Do Not Track, **no cookies, no PII** (only a path + coarse cell counts leave the browser). **Ingest:** `POST /api/heatmap` → `lib/heatmap.ts` aggregates into KV (per-path cell hash via `hincrby`, 90-day rolling TTL, path whitelisted + count-capped). **Render:** the `/admin` **Behaviour** section shows the hottest pages as brand-tinted 24×24 grids (`HeatGrid`), fail-soft to an empty state. Verified in-browser: with consent granted, six clicks bucketed + flushed as one beacon `{path:"/app",cells:[…]}`; the API returns 204; empty-state renders; tsc + eslint clean. KV persistence + the populated grid render confirm on prod (local KV is empty) — checked at the next audit.

## 0.197.0 — 2026-07-11

The in-app composer (`components/blog/PostComposer.tsx`) gets a comma-separated tags input, passed through `POST /api/blog` (accepts an array or a comma string). A series-slug tag surfaces the post on that series' page — consumed in the next change (PR4). Migration applied to prod (Paddock, `eu-west-1`; Management API returned 201, single-transaction). Public reads stay fail-soft so an un-migrated environment degrades to empty, not a crash. Verified: `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` clean; `normalizeTags` edge-case probe (dedupe `F1`→`f1`, kebab `Grand Prix!!`→`grand-prix`, cap 12, truncate 40, non-array→`[]`).

## 0.195.2 — 2026-07-11

### Fixed
- **Race Engineer launcher hidden behind the circuit map.** On `/information/map`, Leaflet's controls sit at `z-index: 1000` and `.leaflet-container` is left at `position: relative; z-index: auto` — which is *not* a stacking context — so those z-1000 values leaked into the root stacking context and painted over the fixed Race Engineer launcher (`z-40`, `components/assistant/AssistantWidget.tsx`) wherever they overlapped (bottom-right, over the attribution control). Added `isolate` (CSS `isolation: isolate`) to the `MapContainer` (`components/information/TracksMapInner.tsx`) so Leaflet's internal z-index stack is bounded inside the map's own stacking context; the launcher — and the sticky header, which had the same latent bug — now win. Root-caused + verified in-browser with a stacking A/B: at the launcher↔attribution overlap, `document.elementFromPoint` returns the launcher with `isolate` and the attribution `<a>` when `isolation` is forced back to `auto`. No z-index change on the widget, so it still sits below modals / the search overlay (`z-50`).

Bumped the cache key to a `v2:` namespace (`lib/wikipedia-bio.ts`) so every bio re-fetches through the identity parser immediately instead of waiting out the TTL. Found by auditing the day's work on prod (evidence: prod `/drivers/max-verstappen` had the Wikipedia "About" section but no `yrs`/flag).

### Fixed
- **Blog posts notify on publish without waiting for the throttled cron** (operator: "blog notifications don't fire on publish"). The publish→push was already wired in `app/api/cron/publish-posts`, but GitHub Actions throttles that `*/15` schedule to ~2h in practice, so the push lagged badly. Extracted the fan-out to `lib/notify-blog.ts` (`announcePublishedPosts` — Next 16 forbids non-handler exports from a `route.ts`) and now call it inline from the approve handler (`app/api/blog/[id]`): approving a post whose `publish_at` has already passed publishes + pushes it immediately. `publishDuePosts` is the status-guarded once-ever flip, so the cron can't re-announce an already-published post; the inline call is best-effort (the cron stays the backstop). Genuinely future-scheduled posts still ride the cron — for reliable sub-daily timing on the current Hobby plan, point an external pinger (e.g. cron-job.org) at the endpoint (see `docs/HANDOFF.md`).

## 0.183.0 — 2026-07-09

### Added
- **Quiet hours** — a per-user do-not-disturb window that pauses ALL push during a nightly range, evaluated in the user's own timezone (captured from the browser on enable). New `quietHours` on `NotifPrefs` (default off) + `isQuietNow()` in `lib/userPrefs.ts` (overnight-wrap aware; fails open on an unparseable tz), a control in `components/NotifPrefsSection.tsx`, and `quietHours` validation in the notif-prefs `PUT`. Every push cron skips a subscriber who's in quiet hours.

### Changed
- **Notification burst coalesced** (operator: "spam all in one minute"). `app/api/cron/notify/route.ts` now fans out per-subscriber: it gathers the tick's queued items each subscriber is eligible for and sends ONE summary push when ≥2 (the single payload for 1, nothing for 0), so a busy 15-min tick lands as one buzz, not up to six. Eligibility + digest are pure, unit-tested `eligibleForNotify` / `coalescedPayload` in `lib/notify-coalesce.ts` — kept out of the route so Next 16's route-type validator only sees the handler.
- **Anonymous subscriptions no longer receive the firehose** — subs with no account (no followed series / prefs to honour) are skipped across all push crons (notify, news, betting, publish-posts, race-week); push now requires sign-in. Fixes anon devices getting every series' notifications unfiltered.

Verified: `isQuietNow` + eligibility unit-tested (`lib/userPrefs.test.ts` + `lib/notify-coalesce.test.ts`, 22 green); `tsc` + full `next build` green. End-to-end push (KV subscriptions + GitHub Actions crons) is observable only on production — watch a busy tick after deploy.
